credentials.description: clientId (API key), provided in the Djomy merchant space
clientSecret (secret key), provided in the Djomy merchant space

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The paymentLinkReference returned by create_payment_link. Passed as a path parameter.

example_prompt: Add a check to see if a customer has paid via the Djomy link I sent them.

response_schema.description: All responses are wrapped in { success, message, data, error, errors, timestamp, status }.

paymentLinkReference.description: Reference of the payment link. Use this (not reference) for all operations.

status.description: ACTIVE = ready to receive payments. REVOKED = manually deactivated. PAID = UNIQUE link that has received one successful payment.

paymentPageUrl.description: Public URL of the payment page.

numberOfUsage.description: Number of successful payments received through this link.

payments.description: List of successful payments made through this link.

gotchas: Fill the {reference} path parameter with paymentLinkReference from create_payment_link, not its deprecated `reference` field ("Merci de considérer le champs paymentLinkReference").

Error codes are distinct (OpenAPI): 404 "Lien de paiement introuvable" (no such link), 403 "Accès non autorisé à ce lien" (a link your credentials may not read), 400 "Format de référence invalide" (a malformed reference). Check the credentials on a 403 and the reference on a 404 or 400.

For UNIQUE links, data.status becomes REVOKED after one successful payment — not PAID. PAID is only set in specific conditions. Use data.numberOfUsage > 0 as the reliable indicator that a UNIQUE link has been used.

The reference comes from your create_payment_link record or from the signed webhook (check X-Webhook-Signature first). If you ever take it from a request (a page URL, a form), validate it before building the path: a visitor can send "../…" and make this call, with your access token, reach another endpoint. The OpenAPI types it as a string with no pattern (its only example is "LINK-REF", in the webhook examples) and documents a 400 "Format de référence invalide" without saying the format, so the example rejects an empty value, ".", any "..", and any /, \, ?, #, %, space or ASCII control character.
A missing or invalid X-API-KEY returns HTTP 401 (documented as "Clé API manquante ou invalide").
open_questions: Production base URL: Djomy's API reference lists only https://sandbox-api.djomy.africa ("Staging environment"). Ask the user or Djomy for the production URL — never guess it.

paymentLinkReference format: the OpenAPI types it as a string with no pattern, gives no example on the field (only "LINK-REF" in the webhook examples) and documents a 400 "Format de référence invalide" — which characters and length can a reference have? Until then the example applies only a generic path-segment guard.
